answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation party statement, NVIDIA Blog, dated 2026-07-01; the source is the company's own announcement. Named partner quotes (Sharon AI CEO James Manning, Firmus co-CEO Tim Rosenfield) are quoted within it, not independently sourced.
answer.note: Material claim: NVIDIA states it is introducing a business model under which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, supported by a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure, with NVIDIA earning standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity. The statement is a forward-looking description by the covered company, with no disclosed dollar amounts, share percentages, credit-support size, contract counts or signed-agreement status. Conditional interpretation: if implemented at scale, the model would add a usage-linked revenue stream on top of hardware sales and could extend NVIDIA's reach into financing-constrained AI cloud capacity. Named examples are plans or expectations: Firmus's Batam campus is described as 'expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs' with no completion date or contract terms given; Sharon AI's collaboration is described qualitatively. The business link from the announcement to NVIDIA's actual revenue, credit exposure or margin is a hypothesis: the quoted facts could all remain true while the revenue-share or credit-support component is small, limited to a few partners, or accounted for in ways that do not affect reported results. The source's use is therefore as a stated strategy and demand/supply lead for NVIDIA-linked AI cloud capacity, not as evidence of realized orders or revenue.
limitations: The revenue-share percentage, credit-support amount, term structure and accounting treatment are not disclosed, so the economic size of the model cannot be estimated from this source.
Whether any AI cloud partner has signed an agreement under the model is not disclosed; the source describes the model and partners' intentions, not executed contracts.
The Firmus 360 MW and up to 170,000 GPU figures are stated as expected scale with no completion date, financing source or NVIDIA-specific commitment.
Sharon AI's and Firmus's relationship to NVIDIA beyond the quoted statements (purchase volumes, credit support received, exclusivity) is not disclosed.
The named AI natives (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) are described as showing demand direction only; no purchase or usage relationship with NVIDIA is stated.
No NVIDIA financial figures for the program are given, so the effect on NVIDIA's reported product revenue, cloud-linked revenue or receivables is unknown.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next periodic SEC filing (10-Q or 10-K) for any disclosure of the revenue-sharing or credit-support model, its scale, related receivables, guarantees or commitments.
Search for signed or announced agreements between NVIDIA and named AI cloud partners (Sharon AI, Firmus) for terms, capacity amounts and any NVIDIA financing or guarantee component.
Check Firmus's and Sharon AI's public filings or press releases for construction timing, financing sources and GPU delivery schedules for the Batam campus and other DSX projects.

Compare the model's terms with any NVIDIA disclosures on customer financing, guarantees or multi-year purchase commitments in prior filings to see whether the credit-support element is new or already reported.
